Lesson 6 of 10 in *Vital, step by step*: everything you need to feel at home in the real Vital plug-in. Short sections, one idea each. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Learn what an LFO is, and its shape and rate.
2. Hear vibrato, a trill-like jump, a sweep and a slow morph.
3. Use LFO 2 and Random through the matrix.
4. Find the real Vital's LFO modes, tempo sync and random styles.
5. Check yourself.
:::

## What an LFO is

- An **LFO** (*low-frequency oscillator*) is an oscillator too slow to hear as a note. You do not listen to it; it moves a knob up and down for you, again and again.
- Its **shape** is how it moves: a *sine* or *triangle* glides smoothly, a *saw* ramps and jumps back, a *square* flips between two places.
- Its **rate** (FREQUENCY) is how fast. On this page, as in Vital, it runs from -7 to 9 (Vital source, synth_parameters.cpp); this page reads that as 2 to the power of the number in hertz (times a second): 0 = once a second, 1 = twice, 3 = 8 times (unverified).

## LFO 1, LFO 2 and Random here

- **LFO 1** has three fixed routes under it: **→ PITCH** (vibrato), **→ CUTOFF** and **→ FRAME**. Or drag its button onto a knob.
- **LFO 2** and **RANDOM 1** are on the MATRIX tab and work through slots only.
- **Random** here jumps to a new random level at each tick of its rate (*sample and hold*). It is this page's own random; Vital's has four styles (below).

## Step by step

Each step loads a starting patch made on this page (not one of Vital's presets) and plays it. Listen for the one thing it names, then turn the knob it names.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;lfoShape&quot;:&quot;sine&quot;,&quot;lfoRate&quot;:2.5,&quot;lfoPitch&quot;:0.4}" data-page="voice"><p><b>Vibrato.</b> LFO 1: sine, rate 2.5 (about 6 times a second), <b>→ PITCH</b> 0.4 semitones. Listen for the singer-like wobble. Raise → PITCH to 2 for a seasick wobble, then back.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;lfoShape&quot;:&quot;square&quot;,&quot;lfoRate&quot;:2,&quot;lfoPitch&quot;:5}" data-page="voice"><p><b>A square jumps.</b> LFO 1: <b>square</b>, rate 2, → PITCH 5 semitones: the pitch flips between two notes, like a trill. Change SHAPE to triangle: it slides between them instead.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;lfoShape&quot;:&quot;saw&quot;,&quot;lfoRate&quot;:1.5,&quot;lfoCut&quot;:30,&quot;cut&quot;:70,&quot;res&quot;:40}" data-page="voice"><p><b>A saw on the cutoff.</b> LFO 1: <b>saw</b>, rate 1.5, <b>→ CUTOFF</b> 30, cutoff 70. Each cycle the filter sweeps one way and snaps back. Listen for the repeating "yow".</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;lfoShape&quot;:&quot;tri&quot;,&quot;lfoRate&quot;:-1,&quot;lfoFrame&quot;:200,&quot;o1Frame&quot;:128}" data-page="voice"><p><b>A slow morph.</b> LFO 1: triangle, rate -1 (once every two seconds), <b>→ FRAME</b> 200, the frame in the middle. Hold a note and hear it morph between soft and bright.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;lfoShape&quot;:&quot;sine&quot;,&quot;lfoRate&quot;:2.4,&quot;lfoPitch&quot;:0.3,&quot;m1s&quot;:&quot;LFO 2&quot;,&quot;m1d&quot;:&quot;Cutoff&quot;,&quot;m1a&quot;:30,&quot;lfo2Shape&quot;:&quot;square&quot;,&quot;lfo2Rate&quot;:2,&quot;cut&quot;:70,&quot;res&quot;:30}" data-page="matrix"><p><b>LFO 2 as well.</b> LFO 1 gives vibrato; slot 1 sends <b>LFO 2</b> (square, rate 2) to the cutoff at 30 %. Two LFOs at two speeds. Change LFO 2's FREQUENCY on the MATRIX tab.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="vital-first" data-set="{&quot;m1s&quot;:&quot;Random&quot;,&quot;m1d&quot;:&quot;Cutoff&quot;,&quot;m1a&quot;:35,&quot;rndRate&quot;:3,&quot;cut&quot;:72,&quot;res&quot;:30}" data-page="matrix"><p><b>Random.</b> Slot 1: <b>Random → Cutoff</b>, 35 %, rate 3. The cutoff jumps to a new place 8 times a second, never in a pattern. Turn RATE down to 0 for one jump a second.</p></div>
```

## In the real Vital

What is different in the plug-in and exactly where to find it. Every line names the file of Vital's source code (github.com/mtytel/vital) it was read from; "(unverified)" means it was not confirmed.

- **Eight LFOs**, LFO 1 to 8, one shown at a time (Vital source, synth_constants.h; modulation_interface.cpp).
- **You draw the shape.** Each LFO is a line editor: double-click empty space to add a point, double-click a point to remove it, drag points to move them, drag a curve handle to bend a line (Vital source, line_editor.cpp). Right-click for Copy, Paste, Flip, Import LFO, Export LFO, Save to LFOs (Vital source, line_editor.cpp). Shapes are saved as `.vitallfo` files and loaded from the name box above the editor (Vital source, synth_constants.h; lfo_section.cpp). The shape a new LFO starts with is not in the notes (unverified).
- **MODE** (how it starts and repeats): Trigger, Sync, Envelope, Sustain Envelope, Loop Point, Loop Hold; it starts on Trigger (Vital source, synth_strings.h; synth_parameters.cpp).
- **FREQUENCY and sync:** next to FREQUENCY you choose Seconds, Tempo, Tempo Dotted, Tempo Triplets or Keytrack. A new LFO starts on **Tempo**, so its speed is a note length such as 1/4 that follows the song's tempo (Vital source, synth_strings.h; synth_parameters.cpp). This page's LFO is free-running in hertz; choose Seconds in Vital to match it.
- **More:** DELAY (wait before it starts), STEREO, and a FADE IN / SMOOTH control (Vital source, lfo_section.cpp).
- **Four randoms:** RANDOM 1 to 4, each with a STYLE: **Perlin**, **Sample & Hold**, **Sine Interpolate**, **Lorenz Attractor**; it starts on Perlin (Vital source, synth_constants.h; synth_strings.h; synth_parameters.cpp). This page's Random is closest to Sample & Hold. Each also has FREQUENCY, STEREO and SYNC (Vital source, random_section.cpp).
- **Using them:** drag the LFO or RANDOM button onto a knob, exactly as in lesson 5.

## Try it in the real Vital

Open Vital in your DAW (see [Meet Vital](intro-vital.qmd) to install it) and do these in order.

- [ ] Initialize the preset. Drag **LFO 1** onto OSC 1's WAVE FRAME. Listen.
- [ ] In LFO 1's editor, double-click to add a point and drag it. Hear the movement change.
- [ ] Set LFO 1's sync to **Seconds** and turn FREQUENCY. Then try **Tempo** and pick 1/8.
- [ ] Change MODE to **Envelope** and play: it runs once per note.
- [ ] Click RANDOM 1, set STYLE to **Sample & Hold** and drag it onto CUTOFF (with FILTER 1 on).

## Check yourself

Click an answer. You will see at once if it is right. Nothing is saved or sent.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What does an LFO do?</b></p><ul><li>Moves a knob up and down over and over</li><li>Plays the melody</li><li>Saves the preset</li><li>Adds echo</li></ul><p class="ik-why">It is a slow oscillator used to move other controls.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Vibrato is an LFO on…</b></p><ul><li>Pitch</li><li>Volume only</li><li>Reverb</li><li>Polyphony</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Step 1.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>A square-shaped LFO on pitch sounds like…</b></p><ul><li>Jumps between two notes</li><li>A smooth glide</li><li>Silence</li><li>A chord</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Step 2.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>A new LFO in the real Vital is synced to…</b></p><ul><li>Tempo (note lengths)</li><li>Seconds</li><li>Keytrack</li><li>Nothing</li></ul><p class="ik-why">LFO "sync" defaults to Tempo (synth_parameters.cpp).</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Which is one of the real Vital&#x27;s random styles?</b></p><ul><li>Perlin</li><li>Sawtooth</li><li>Reverb</li><li>Ladder</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Perlin, Sample &amp; Hold, Sine Interpolate, Lorenz Attractor (synth_strings.h).</p></div>
```
